## Verdict

Inkwell costs least for a team of 9, at $80 per month. Its 10-seat minimum means the team pays for one seat it will not use, and even so it undercuts Dorado's $171 and Borealis's $300.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Dorado | $19 | 1 |
| Inkwell | $8 | 10 |
| Borealis | $12 | 25 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for is the team size (9) or the vendor minimum, whichever is larger.

- **Dorado:** minimum 1 is below 9, so 9 seats paid. 9 × $19 = **$171 per month**.
- **Inkwell:** minimum 10 exceeds 9, so 10 seats paid. 10 × $8 = **$80 per month**. One unused seat, worth $8.
- **Borealis:** minimum 25 exceeds 9, so 25 seats paid. 25 × $12 = **$300 per month**. Sixteen unused seats, worth $192.

Inkwell is $91 per month cheaper than Dorado and $220 cheaper than Borealis — $1,092 and $2,640 over twelve months.

## Risks

Inkwell's padded seat gives it an effective rate of $8.89 per person ($80 ÷ 9), still less than half Dorado's $19. That penalty disappears entirely at 10 people and never returns above that size, so the ranking holds as the team grows. Borealis stays the dearest option until 25 seats, at which point it costs $300 against Inkwell's $200 — so it does not overtake Inkwell on list price at any size here.

A shrinking team changes things. Below about 4 people Dorado becomes cheaper than Inkwell's $80 floor, since Dorado bills only for seats used.

This compares price and nothing else. The price list carries no detail on features, support tiers, usage limits or security, so a cheaper seat may not be a comparable product. All figures assume monthly billing as stated; annual terms, discounts and onboarding fees are not listed and could reorder the result.
